instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Converted back to a forward after joining Ipswich.

An ever-present at the centre of the meanest defence outside the top four; commanding in the air and a genuine international-standard centre-half.
Thirty-four and displaced by Cudicini; six starts in his last Chelsea season.
Capped by England in 1991; this was his comeback season after a cruciate injury.
Thirty-one, four starts, and three seasons after his last regular top-flight football; the pace that made the crossing dangerous had gone.
A genuine late developer — a fringe player at 24, a first-choice Premier League midfielder at 30.
Captain of a Southampton side that reached the FA Cup final; a genuinely useful left-sided midfielder at 33, and no more than that.
Twelve league goals and comfortably Fulham’s best attacker; the season the running and the finishing arrived together.
Still the best left foot in the squad, but the application and the end product both dropped.
Three seasons at Celtic in between; back in England at 30 with the vision intact and the sharpness reduced - eight assists in a mid-table City side.
Four goals in 24 starts for a Bradford side relegated with 26 points; the least effective season of a modest top-flight career.
Thirteen goals as a 22-year-old in Reading’s first top-flight season; the running and the hold-up play were the real ability, the goals a by-product.
Six years and a spell at Marseille apart; the 20-year-old at Oldham and the established Sunderland right-back are not the same footballer.
Three starts; lost the shirt amid the match-fixing trial.

Athletic, quick, comfortable on the ball and a South Africa regular; clearly better than the Bolton side around him.

On loan from Real Madrid and Middlesbrough’s best player: seven goals and eight assists, most of them from set pieces.

Thirty-four, seven starts, and the eleven-point Derby side around him; below the level he held at Coventry.
Six starts only; the ankle and groin trouble that wrecked his career.
A 2002 World Cup star and Ligue 1 champion in his first English season; physically dominant in midfield and a real threat arriving in the box.
Five starts; injury rather than form kept him out of the Everton side that finished fourth.

Squeezed out by City’s spending and visibly off the level of the year before.
A peripheral figure at Villa after the City move, and a long way from the player of 2008/09.
Four starts across a season lost to injury; thirty, and effectively finished as a regular.
